sourceConclusions: Current ordinary JMdict uses full metadata input; its active wrapper bulk-copies metadata/identity/rows/signatures instead of executing the unique-metadata per-row JS packing loop.
All 3,998 ordinary exact candidates were recent-source hits, so this observed workload has no exact-read OPFS round trip to remove.
The qualified source-derived acquisition used one fixed 26,214,400-byte arena/one native instance. The separate ordinary browser capacity counter was 1.9 ms; no cross-boundary subtraction is made.

Common block-storage publication returns scalar compact-block codec, Float64 offsets and Uint32 lengths. Deferred resolution separately allocates all three targets; native pending indexes are separately allocated and sliced to count. Source supports eligibility but the CPU trace does not prove every runtime branch.

The eligible resolved-plan helper has one pending-index run-discovery pass, then required offset/length copies and flag fills; codec and alias guards are per-call. Small-run allocation reduction lacks evidence of material absolute benefit.
